## Headline

I wrote notes/procedure.md and applied it to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md, and all three now pass check_file.

- The procedure has 10 numbered steps: read, check, rewrite, write, and check again.
- notes/a.md and notes/c.md had one banned booster each, and I removed it.
- notes/b.md and notes/c.md had one long sentence each, and I split it.

## Background

The request asked for a procedure first, then three file fixes in a set order. The tools were read_file, check_file, and write_file. Each file had to keep its meaning.

## Relevance

Clean notes meet the style limits in Section 4. The procedure lets any agent repeat the fix.

## Information

Evidence from check_file, a tool run in this session:

- notes/a.md: 1 banned word ("clearly"). After the fix: 0 banned words, 0 long sentences.
- notes/b.md: 1 sentence over 25 words. After the fix: 0 long sentences.
- notes/c.md: 1 banned word ("very") and 1 long sentence. After the fix: 0 of each.

Each rewrite keeps every fact. I removed the boosters and split the long sentences at their clauses. The only added words are the links "Then", "Last", and "This way". [judgment]

Assumption: the check_file tool is the full test of style. Why not measured: no tool can reach a human review of meaning. Validate by: read each file once more. If wrong: edit the files again.

## End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the standard method for note fixes. Increment: one file, already written. Blocker removed: no shared method. Test (deterministic): Given a note with a banned word, When an agent follows Steps 1 to 10, Then check_file reports no failures. Domain: Clear, because deduction from a known rule applies.
2. Run check_file on every notes file before each release. Increment: one pass over the folder. Blocker removed: unseen style failures. Test (deterministic): Given the notes folder, When check_file runs on each file, Then every report shows an empty failures list. Domain: Clear, because the tool gives a fixed result.
3. Have a person review the meaning of the three rewrites. Increment: one read of three short files. Blocker removed: tool checks cannot judge meaning. Test (evaluative): the rubric is "all facts kept" at weight 100%, pass threshold 100%, evidence is a side-by-side read. Domain: Complicated, because analysis of the old and new text decides the result.

Step 3 MUST NOT start until the test in Step 2 passes.

## Follow-up

No open questions. If the review in Step 3 finds a lost fact, restore that fact and run check_file again.

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file

1. Call read_file on the file. Save the full text.
2. Call check_file on the same path. Record each banned word and each long sentence.
3. Stop if the report shows no banned words and no long sentences.
4. Rewrite each banned word. Use a plain word, or delete the word if the sentence keeps its meaning.
5. Split each long sentence into shorter sentences. Keep each sentence at 20 words or fewer.
6. Check that the new text keeps every fact, number, name, and instruction of the old text.
7. Call write_file with the full new text. The call replaces the old file.
8. Call check_file again on the same path.
9. If the report still shows a problem, go back to Step 4. Repeat until the report is clean.
10. Call read_file once more. Confirm that the meaning is the same.
